newsitem.title: INDIA: Pakistan hopeful talks with India to move forward.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan hopeful talks with India to move forward.

text.p: Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan was quoted on Tuesday as saying Islamabad hoped peace talks with New Delhi would move forward even if Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government fell.

Khan told Cable News Network (CNN) television in an interview that three wars between the two neighbouring countries could have been avoided, and that Pakistan would not allow the fresh peace talks which began last month to fail.
Khan was asked how a political crisis threatening Deve Gowda's government affected the bilateral dialogue.

"By and large the foreign policy of India may not undergo a drastic change," Khan said, according to a transcript of the interview released by CNN. "We are hopeful whichever government there is, existing or a new government, that we'd continue this dialogue in a fruitful manner."

Khan said three wars since 1947 between the two countries did not achieve much. "Pakistan today is in a position to talk on substantial issues," he said. "We should talk and talk, and that's what we'll do. We'll talk, we will not allow the talks to break."

The Pakistani minister, who was to meet Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Wednesday, urged New Delhi to reduce the number of security forces in Kashmir as a "starter" towards settling a longstanding dispute over the region.
